observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: The receiver arrives in ECX and is forwarded to the single callee unchanged: there is no MOV ECX anywhere in the body before the CALL at 0x00b25c4c, and the CALL is followed by MOV ESI,EAX, not by any use of ECX as an input. The frame is PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI with the mirror POP sequence and a bare RET at 0x00b25c89, 0x00b25c92 and the fallthrough, so there are no stack arguments of its own and the caller owns cleanup.
observed_original_abi.return_type: pointer to a registry element, or null
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: The address of the first array element whose embedded interface at byte offset +0x120 answers true through vtable slot +0x58. If the element count is not positive, or if no element matches, the return is 0. The success path explicitly re-reads the element pointer from the array after restoring the saved registers, so the returned value is the element pointer itself and not the interface sub-object.
observed_original_abi.return_observation: 0x00b25c86 XOR EAX,EAX is the failure return; 0x00b25c8a MOV ECX,[ESI] followed by 0x00b25c8c MOV EAX,[ECX + EBX*0x4] is the success return, re-loading elements[i]. No caller-visible transformation is applied.
observed_original_abi.frame: PUSH EBX ; PUSH ESI ; PUSH EDI, mirrored by POP EDI ; POP ESI ; POP EBX on both exits; no SUB ESP and no EBP frame
observed_original_abi.hidden_receiver: read once, forwarded to the callee in ECX

observed_mechanics: 0x00b25c33..0x00b25c47 push five immediates. Because arguments are pushed right to left the callee signature is arg1 = 0x018c43e8, arg2 = 0x00b1e500, arg3 = 0x00acdff0, arg4 = 0x00d3d420, arg5 = 0x00cd7d10.

0x018c43e8 is a .bss dword that reads 0 in the file image, so it is a runtime-populated key; the other four are code addresses, all of which exist as instructions in .text: 0x00b1e500 is MOV ECX,[ESP + 0x4] ; MOV EAX,[ECX] ; MOV EDX,[EAX + 0x20] ; CALL EDX ; CMP EAX,[ESP + 0x8] ; SETZ CL ; MOV AL,CL ; RET, and 0x00d3d420 is MOV ECX,[ESP + 0x4] ; MOV EAX,[ECX + 0x8] ; MOV EDX,[ECX + 0x4] ; ADD ECX,0x4 ; PUSH EAX ; PUSH EDX ; CALL 0x00e25bd0 ; RET, and 0x00acdff0 is MOV ECX,[ESP + 0x8] ; TEST ECX,ECX ; JZ ; MOV EAX,[ECX] ; MOV EDX,[EAX + 0xc] ; PUSH 0xee9b2232 ; CALL EDX.

0x00b25c4c CALL 0x00b21340 with ECX untouched. The relative displacement was verified from the raw bytes e8 ef b6 ff ff at 0x00b25c4c, giving target 0x00b25c4c + 5 + 0xffffffb6 = 0x00b21340, so the ledger's callee identity is correct.

0x00b21340 is itself a __thiscall with RET 0x14, i.e. five stack dwords, and internally uses a map at this+0x98 and a singly linked list at this+0x78. It is kept as an opaque port; no part of its body is reconstructed here.

0x00b25c53..0x00b25c5c: the container's +0x8 minus its +0x4 is a byte span, SAR by 2 turns it into a SIGNED element count, and ADD ESI,0x4 moves ESI onto the element array so that [ESI + EBX*4] indexes it directly.
0x00b25c61 TEST EDI,EDI with 0x00b25c63 JBE is a signed comparison on the SARed count, so both a zero count and a NEGATIVE span take the early exit at 0x00b25c84 and return 0.
0x00b25c65..0x00b25c67 load elements[i] in two steps: MOV EAX,[ESI] reads the array base and MOV EAX,[EAX + EBX*4] reads the i-th pointer out of it.

0x00b25c6a MOV EDX,[EAX + 0x120] reads the vtable of an interface embedded at byte offset 0x120 inside the element, and 0x00b25c70 LEA ECX,[EAX + 0x120] makes that same sub-object the receiver, so the dispatched method operates on the interface and not on the element.
0x00b25c76 MOV EAX,[EDX + 0x58] then 0x00b25c79 CALL EAX is the only virtual dispatch, at slot offset +0x58.
0x00b25c7b TEST AL,AL with 0x00b25c7d JNZ 0x00b25c8a means a NON-ZERO answer selects the element; the predicate is a truth test on AL, not on the full EAX.
0x00b25c7f..0x00b25c82 is the loop back-edge: INC EBX ; CMP EBX,EDI ; JC. JC is unsigned, but the count was already proved positive at 0x00b25c63, so the two comparisons agree.
0x00b25c8a..0x00b25c8c re-reads the element pointer from the array rather than keeping it in a register, so the returned value is provably elements[i] and not the interface sub-object.
0x00b25c86 XOR EAX,EAX is the sole failure return, and both exits restore the three saved registers in the mirror order.
The body has exactly one non-virtual CALL and exactly one virtual CALL, no global read and no field write.

semantic_contract: Obtain a registry entry from the receiver and return the first element of that entry's array that satisfies a per-element predicate. Concretely: call the receiver's get-or-create helper 0x00b21340 with five caller-supplied callback or key immediates, forwarding the receiver in ECX; read the returned container's element array from its +0x4 and +0x8 members and divide the byte span by 4 to get a signed element count; if that count is not positive, return 0. Otherwise walk the array in order and, for each element, dispatch vtable slot +0x58 of the interface embedded at byte offset +0x120 inside that element, with the interface sub-object as the receiver. The first element whose predicate returns a non-zero AL is returned immediately as elements[i]; if the array is exhausted without a match, return 0. The function writes no field and no global, saves and restores EBX/ESI/EDI, and makes exactly one non-virtual call and one virtual call. It does not null-check the container the helper returns.
classification_rationale: Not STRONG_SEMANTIC: the body, the ABI, the element-count derivation, the loop bound, the branch polarity, the slot offset +0x58, the receiver sub-object offset +0x120 and the return-value identity are all read directly from live disassembly and corroborated by a sibling that walks the same container with the same helper, but the owning class, the element type, the concrete callee behind slot +0x58 and the semantics of the single callee 0x00b21340 are unestablished, and those are material elements. Not STRUCTURAL_ONLY: the selection contract - first match wins, scan stops there, non-positive count yields null - is a genuine behavioural claim and is fully reconstructed. The bound is named: owning type, element type, slot +0x58 implementation, and the callee's element type.
semantic_findings: The receiver is forwarded to the callee in ECX without being touched, which is why the function needs no argument of its own and why all 26 callsites are uniform: CALL 0x00b3d300 ; MOV ECX,EAX ; CALL 0x00b25c30. The global manager at 0x0167eae0 is therefore the proven receiver source.

The count is derived with SAR, not SHR, and the guard is JBE, so a container whose end precedes its begin also exits early with 0 instead of scanning a huge unsigned count. The model test pins both the zero and the negative span.

The loop back-edge uses unsigned JC while the guard uses signed JBE; the two agree only because the guard has already proved the count positive, which is a real invariant of the reconstruction rather than an accident.

The selection is first-match, not first-non-match: 0x00b25c7d JNZ on TEST AL,AL leaves the loop on a non-zero answer and 0x00b25c8a re-reads elements[i] rather than keeping a register copy, so the returned pointer is provably the array element.
The predicate is dispatched on the interface at element+0x120, not on the element itself, so the selection logic is defined by a sub-object that the element merely carries.

The five callee immediates are a per-callsite configuration, not code constants: 0x018c43e8 is a runtime .bss key that reads 0 in the file, and the four code addresses differ between this function and the sibling 0x00fef3b0, which uses 0x02aa5ada, 0x00b1e520, 0x00fed010, 0x00d3d420 and 0x00cd7d10. Two of the five are shared, three are per-callsite.

0x00b1e500, one of the callbacks, is itself a virtual dispatcher: it loads a vtable, calls slot +0x20 and compares the result against its second argument with SETZ, i.e. it is an equality predicate over a runtime key. The callback set as a whole is a get-or-create configuration, which is why the helper is best kept as a port.

Two callers, 0x00bf4fc0 and 0x00e07e70, use the returned element as a receiver for further calls (0x00bd81d0, 0x00bd9b40, 0x00bd7df0) and read its +0x34, so the element is a large polymorphic object, not a small record.

The briefing recorded 18 callers; the live xref query returns 26 UNCONDITIONAL_CALL references, so four further callsites exist at 0x00cee1f3, 0x00cfd794, 0x00cfd7b7 and 0x00ea72e1. None is a DATA reference, so the function still occupies no vtable slot.
unresolved_questions: What class owns this function? 26 live references, all UNCONDITIONAL_CALL, and no DATA reference, so it is not a vtable slot and no owner can be named.
What is the concrete callee at vtable slot +0x58 of the element's +0x120 interface? No element instance and therefore no table address was ever observed statically.

What is the element type, and what is the interface at element+0x120? Only the vtable load and the slot offset are observed. Callers show the element itself is polymorphic with an interface at +0x34 whose slot +0x48 is dispatched at 0x00e08285, so the element carries at least two embedded interfaces.

What does the get-or-create helper 0x00b21340 actually do, and what is its element type? Its map at this+0x98 and list at this+0x78 and its five callbacks are observed, but no element type was established, so it is kept as an opaque port rather than guessed.

Which of the five immediates is the lookup key and which are callbacks? The push order and the callee's five-argument frame are established, but the per-argument role assignment inside 0x00b21340 was not fully resolved and is therefore not asserted.
What is the runtime value of the .bss key 0x018c43e8? It reads 0 in the file image and is populated only at runtime.
Is the container returned by the helper ever null? The body dereferences it immediately at 0x00b25c53, so a null return would fault; the reconstruction preserves that rather than adding a guard.
What are the four unreported callsites at 0x00cee1f3, 0x00cfd794, 0x00cfd7b7 and 0x00ea72e1, which lie outside any Ghidra function body?
No original-process trace exists, so the runtime contents of the registry and the real distribution of predicate answers are unverified.

body_reconstruction.claim_scope: The 99-byte body is reconstructed in full, including the five callee immediates in push order, the signed count derivation, the non-positive-count early exit, the first-match selection and the identity of the returned pointer. The single callee and the virtual slot are declared as explicitly named opaque ports; no class, element type or slot name is claimed, and the absent null check on the callee's return is preserved rather than defended against.
